docs.title: Guided Data Import, Templates, and Configurable Exports

sections.text: ERPForAll provides a built-in **Import / Export** menu on list views so teams can onboard master data (such as Contacts, Products, Chart of Accounts, or Opening Balances) from spreadsheets with pre-built templates and dry-run validation, or export filtered lists into configurable **CSV** and **Excel (.xlsx)** files.

1. Open the list view for the records you want to import (for example, **Contacts**, **Sales → Products → Products**, or **Accounting → Configuration → Chart of Accounts**). 2. Click **Import / Export** beside the **+ New** button and choose **Import records**. 3. Click **Download Excel (.xlsx) template** or **Download CSV (.csv) template** to get a ready-to-fill spreadsheet containing valid column headers (models such as **Contacts** also include a guided sample layout). 4. Populate your rows in Excel, LibreOffice Calc, or Google Sheets while keeping the header row intact. ![The guided Import records dialog provides one-click Excel and CSV templates together with a drag-and-drop file upload zone.](/en/next/assets/docs/assets/user-manual/getting-started/guided-import-dialog.webp)

1. In the **Import records** dialog, drag and drop your .csv or .xlsx file (maximum **10 MB**) or click to browse from your computer. 2. **Select Worksheet (.xlsx only)**: If your Excel workbook contains multiple sheets, choose the sheet holding your data to preview its rows. 3. **Review Column Mapping**: * ERPForAll automatically matches exact technical field names first, followed by unambiguous field labels, and previews the first rows directly in the dialog. * Technical relation paths (such as parent_id/name or category_id/.id) are preserved and validated against the server. * For any unmatched column, choose the target ERP field from the column dropdown or leave it unmapped to skip that column. 4. **Run Dry-Run Validation (Test)**: * Click **Test** before committing changes. ERPForAll validates every row—checking required fields, data types, company rules, and relational links—without writing to the database. * Fix any reported row-level errors in your file or column mapping and re-run **Test** until validation passes cleanly. 5. **Commit Records (Import)**: * Click **Import** to create or update the records in one validated batch. Once complete, ERPForAll shows the imported count and refreshes the list view automatically.

1. Open any list view and apply search filters, group-bys, or check specific rows if you want to export a subset. 2. Click **Import / Export → Export**. 3. Choose the **Export format**: * **CSV (.csv)**: Lightweight UTF-8 text file ideal for scripts and system integrations. * **Excel (.xlsx)**: Native spreadsheet workbook with formatted column headers ready for business analysis. 4. Select, add, remove, or reorder the fields you want included in the exported file. 5. Click **Export** to download the file immediately.

* **Always Run Test First**: Dry-run validation catches missing required fields, bad dates, or unknown relational names before any record is saved. * **Respect the 10 MB Upload Limit**: For very large migrations, split spreadsheets into smaller batches (for example, 2,000–5,000 rows per file) to keep validation fast and easy to audit. * **Import Parent Records Before Children**: Import Companies before individual child Contacts, Product Categories before Products, and Products before Opening Stock or Orders so relational lookups resolve on the first pass. * **Access Rights Apply**: Import and export respect your exact model, record, and company access permissions; you can only import records you are authorized to create or write.

Report templates choose the code type. Data Matrix and QR are different formats: a Data Matrix request prints a square ECC200 symbol, including when the template calls it ECC200DataMatrix. The renderer does not replace a failed code with another format. Available report and label choices depend on the installed addons; encoder support does not add a label-printing wizard.

Print at actual size and keep the blank margin around the symbol clear. Data Matrix includes a one-module margin and no text caption. Ask the report author to match the template's printer resolution to your printer. If the code does not fit, enlarge its box; do not stretch the PDF. Use a scanner configured for Data Matrix. Ordinary codes can carry Unicode, but scanner handling of character encoding varies. Check the scanned value against the original record on your own printer and scanner before using a label layout operationally. Hardware compatibility is not established by the report encoder.

GS1 Data Matrix and GS1-128 require an explicit template option; a numeric prefix alone does not enable it. The report author supplies the GS1 element string, validates its application identifiers and check digits, and places any group separators. The encoder adds the GS1 marker and preserves the supplied data. It accepts printable ASCII and group separators in this mode; other characters fail.

Extended39 carries lowercase letters and other ASCII characters. Configure your scanner for full-ASCII Code39; ordinary Code39 remains limited to its standard alphabet. Control characters appear as visible hexadecimal escapes in the printed caption, while the code retains the original data. ITF14 includes top and bottom bearer bars. The report author can set their thickness from 2 to 10 narrow modules. They fit inside the code's box; if the box is too short, rendering stops with an error. This supports non-plate printing. Confirm the physical label dimensions required by your trading partner; encoder support alone does not certify a label for every GS1 application.

An unsupported value, excessive length or a box too small stops rendering with an error. Give the report author the error and the affected record so they can correct the value or template. The renderer does not silently shorten the value or switch to QR, Code 128 or plain text.
